svg.title: The write path and the read path
svg.desc: How a text memory works, as two paths around a store. The write path runs after or during a conversation and can run in the background: consolidation turns the conversation into candidate memories ("I moved to Berlin in May" becomes "lives in Berlin, since May 2026"); updating reconciles each one with what is stored (it replaces "lives in Munich"); indexing builds what a read will use, such as an embedding or a keyword index. Forgetting drops or decays entries in the store. The read path runs on every request while the user waits: retrieval finds what the request needs ("any good bakeries near me?" finds "lives in Berlin"), and condensation shortens it to fit the prompt. The answering model gets the instructions, what memory returned, and the request. Each operation is tagged with the survey's group: encoding, evolving or adapting.
